meta.method: Exterior-first architectural pass. A candidate had to be an individually documented building or facade, have authoritative evidence that the whole street-facing composition belongs to Art Nouveau rather than merely carrying one period detail, remain legible from an ordinary public route during the visit window, and survive exact-coordinate, alias, external-ID and 120-metre global catalogue review.
meta.quality_policy: All retained rows are all-high draft candidates. Exterior viewing is the experience; no interior access is promised. Temporary scaffolding is the only same-day condition that cannot be guaranteed remotely and should be field-checked.
meta.category_decision: artnouveau is coherent and globally reusable as a strict exterior-architecture lane. It does not absorb living religious buildings, active venues whose exterior is incidental, interiors, isolated decorative fragments, generic Belle Epoque buildings or serial Guimard street furniture.
meta.strict_stop: The run stops at 11. Seven source-plausible buildings were deferred and 15 were excluded rather than padding the category with famous defaults, interior-led places or token motifs.

artnouveau.label: Art Nouveau
artnouveau.definition: A named or individually documented building whose whole street-facing architectural composition is authoritatively identified as Art Nouveau or a direct regional equivalent, and whose exterior is itself the pavement-visible experience.
include: complete, individually documented Art Nouveau facades and buildings
regional equivalents such as Jugendstil, Secession, Modernisme and Liberty when the whole exterior composition qualifies
street-visible organic line, structural expression and integrated ceramic, iron, stone, mosaic or sculptural programmes
private buildings when the exterior alone supplies a worthwhile public-route encounter
exclude: generic Belle Epoque or eclectic facades with one curving door, floral panel or other token motif
Art Nouveau interiors behind conventional exteriors
isolated doors, mosaics, stained glass or shop fittings on buildings of another primary style
repetitive civic objects and Guimard Metro entrances, which belong to streetfurniture
living religious buildings, where synagogue, church, mosque or another current-use category wins
active venues where the exterior is incidental to the current-use experience
district-scale ensembles and serial address padding
global_reuse: Glasgow Style and other individually documented regional equivalents

included.s: A lace designer gave Guimard a house whose gate and facade behave like one continuous drawn line—years before the planned museum arrives.
included.q: Hôtel Mezzara 60 rue Jean de La Fontaine Paris
included.w: Read the curves from the street grille through the asymmetric openings rather than waiting for an interior visit. The textile commission matters: Guimard designed this 1910–1911 house for Paul Mezzara, a lace-pattern creator, and the building's promised museum will not open until 2028.

facts.claim: Hector Guimard built the house in 1910–1911 for Paul Mezzara.
Paul Mezzara was a textile industrialist and creator of lace patterns.
The state announced a Guimard and Art Nouveau museum here for January 2028 after works, so it is not an open museum during the August 2026 visit.

included.s: Guimard squeezed his office, home and his wife's studio onto a 90-square-metre triangular plot.
included.w: The irregular windows and swelling bays are the plan made visible: six levels forced onto an awkward wedge. Start at the monumental entrance, then follow the floral stone and ironwork upward to see how Guimard turned constraint into movement.

Guimard used six levels, projecting bays and irregular openings to fit the programme onto the constrained site.

included.w: The remarkable Art Nouveau facade belongs to a social building, not a decorative palace: reinforced concrete, light courts and setbacks were designed around hygiene and comfort. The current complex contains 350 lodgings for about 400 people.
The building remains permanently occupied.

verification.source_rule: 11/11 retained rows have at least two useful sources and at least one official heritage, municipal or current land-manager source. Every factual claim links only to a URL present in that row's source bundle.
verification.coordinate_rule: 11/11 pins were independently resolved to named-building object locations, not neighbourhood or photographer positions; address and coordinate corroboration were compared source by source.
verification.access_rule: 11/11 are ordinary public-pavement exterior views for 13–16 August 2026 and do not depend on interior, school, hotel, theatre, worship or public-holiday opening. Temporary scaffolding remains a same-day field check.
verification.score_rule: All totals are 23–25; every story and walkability component is at least 4; every confidence dimension is high.
verification.global_dedupe: All 17,328 production rows were checked at a 120-metre radius using exact pins, then names, aliases and external IDs were reviewed. Two 30–119-metre cases were retained only after explicit distinct-object review: Hôtel Guimard versus Studio Building at 83 m, and the former grocery syndicate versus Fontaine Stravinsky at 100 m.
verification.current_wave_dedupe: All available Paris 2026-08-09 dossiers were checked. The only sub-120-metre current-wave encounters reproduce the same two production objects already reviewed; no candidate duplicates another current-wave addition.
verification.internal_spacing: No two retained Art Nouveau candidates are within 120 metres. The closest retained pair is Hôtel Mezzara–Hôtel Guimard at 325 m. The screened 14–16 rue d'Abbeville pair is about 40 m, so no. 16 was excluded.
verification.category_precedence: Synagogue Agoudas Hakehilos remains synagogue. Guimard authorship and Art Nouveau style belong in searchable facts, while the specific living congregation category wins primary classification.
verification.production_state: The category was registered and the 11 retained rows were imported once as quality-d drafts. Do not reimport or promote them before field testing and editorial review.
